hints: For every number you print exactly one thing. Which case must you test first so that 15 does not get printed as just Tick?
A single loop from 1 to N with an if / else-if chain. Check divisibility with the remainder operator %, testing the 'both' case (divisible by 15) before the single cases.

1. Loop i from 1 to N.
  2. If i % 15 == 0 add TickTock.
  3. Else if i % 3 == 0 add Tick.
  4. Else if i % 5 == 0 add Tock.
  5. Else add the number itself.
  6. Print all lines at the end (one StringBuilder is faster than many prints).

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: One pass from 1 to N, deciding each line with the remainder checks in the right order.

explain: For N = 15 the loop prints 1, 2, then Tick for 3, Tock for 5, and so on. At 15 both 3 and 5 divide it, so the first branch (i % 15 == 0) must catch it; if you tested % 3 first you would print Tick and never reach the combined case. The order of the if-chain is the whole trick. Collect lines in a StringBuilder and print once to keep it fast.
recognize: Print something different depending on which numbers divide i → a loop with an ordered if / else-if chain on %.
